items.text: Judge Loren AliKhan of the federal district court in D.C. granted ABC a preliminary injunction blocking the FCC's early review of the licences of ABC's eight owned TV stations, finding ABC likely to win its First Amendment retaliation claim. She called it not a close case and cited public statements by Trump and FCC Chair Brendan Carr, writing that Carr treated Trump's rhetoric as marching orders and that the review was already chilling ABC's coverage and guest booking. The FCC ordered the early reviews on April 28 after a Jimmy Kimmel joke Trump objected to. The FCC called the ruling wrong on the facts and the law and said it will keep holding broadcasters accountable; the order does not bar future FCC reviews. Democratic Commissioner Anna Gomez welcomed it.
items.notes: Ruling issued Wednesday Nov 25; covered by TIME, The Hill, Variety, NBC. Whether the FCC will appeal is not yet stated.

items.text: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, the Salvadoran man wrongly deported to El Salvador in 2025, left the US on a commercial flight on Nov 24 and arrived in Madrid on Nov 25 with his wife and lawyer. Judge Paula Xinis had ordered the government to ensure his unimpeded departure, lift any holds and remove his ankle monitor; after he left she closed the civil case and dissolved her injunctions. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said he self-deported under a removal order, got no incentives and will never be allowed back; DHS repeats its gang claim, which his lawyers deny. Smuggling charges against him were dismissed in May as vindictive; DOJ's appeal is set for Sixth Circuit argument in February.
items.notes: Not previously logged. He entered Spain on his Salvadoran passport, per his lawyer.

items.text: A federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Huawei and three subsidiaries (Huawei Device, Futurewei and Huawei Device USA) on 10 of 12 counts, including bank and wire fraud, money-laundering conspiracy, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and violating Iran sanctions. They were acquitted of racketeering conspiracy and obstruction conspiracy. Sentencing is set for Sept 14, 2027, with fines, forfeiture and restitution possible. AG Todd Blanche said no company is above the law; Huawei said the remaining convictions lack legal merit and it will defend its rights.
items.notes: Verdict Nov 24, missed in earlier logs. DOJ press release exists but could not be fetched (permission timeout). No Chinese government reaction found.

items.text: AG Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel announced what they called the largest anti-scam enforcement surge in history: more than 400 cases in 85 federal districts, over 800 defendants charged, extradited, convicted or sentenced, and over $8 billion in intended victim losses recovered. The FBI's Operation Blackout targeted scam compounds abroad, with 29 compounds disrupted on four continents and more than 2,200 trafficking victims freed, according to the department. Cases cover impersonation of officials, sextortion of minors and sales of elderly people's data to fraud rings. The effort follows a March executive order on cybercrime and fraud.
items.notes: Figures are DOJ claims; the DOJ release could not be fetched. Missed in earlier logs (announced Nov 24).

items.text: The Washington Post, citing three people familiar with the talks, reported that War Secretary Pete Hegseth, Deputy Secretary Steve Feinberg and Under Secretary Emil Michael discussed using the Defense Production Act to pressure Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang, for example by threatening to shift production to military work. The Post describes a Cabinet-level weekend push before the Nov 23 reinstatement. A Pentagon official said the discussions never happened and no such proposal was made; the White House referred questions to the Pentagon and Nvidia declined to comment. Experts quoted said the law does not clearly allow such use.
items.notes: Anonymous-source report; Pentagon denial. Read via Yahoo syndication of WaPo (published Nov 26 04:33 UTC).

items.text: A coast-to-coast Thanksgiving storm system brought heavy rain, high winds and flooding, leaving more than 900,000 homes and businesses without power on Thursday evening, mostly on the East Coast (poweroutage.us). New Jersey (Gov. Sherrill declared a statewide emergency on Nov 25) and parts of New York were under states of emergency, and FlightAware counted over 2,000 delayed and 400 cancelled US flights. Macy's postponed its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday Nov 28 over wind gusts, the first weather postponement in its history. Parts of Missouri got up to 35 cm of snow, and record king tides flooded the California coast from Humboldt to Ventura counties, forcing evacuations.
items.notes: No deaths reported in the AP account read. NJ link is the governor's emergency declaration (not fetched).

items.text: The Army detonated nearly five tons of degraded lead azide (68 barrels) at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown on Nov 25 after evacuating nearby residents and telling people downwind, up to about 40 miles away, to stay indoors; some 350 farms in Iowa and Missouri were potentially affected. The EPA said its real-time monitors detected zero airborne lead, and the shelter-in-place order was later lifted. EPA and the Army are now taking post-blast samples to measure how much lead was released, and the Army has opened a claims page.

Judge Dana Sabraw (S.D. Cal.) issued two orders in Fanfan v. Mullin restricting ICE from re-detaining immigrants in San Diego and Imperial counties who were released and are complying with mandatory check-ins, unless officials show their circumstances changed materially, such as new danger or flight risk. People subject to mandatory detention are excluded and the orders are not nationwide. They stay in force while the case proceeds.
items.notes: Main account is Matzav (no wire attribution); UCLA Law (plaintiffs' counsel) lists a Nov 25 release on the order. No DHS comment found. Exact date 'Tuesday' = Nov 24.

items.text: Judge Anthony Mattivi of the federal court in Kansas set a Nov 30 hearing on Fort Hood gunman Nidal Hasan's motion to stay his Dec 3 execution so he can seek federal habeas review. Hasan, who killed 13 people in 2009, filed on Nov 24 and also asked for added counsel; the government opposes. Filings are due Nov 27 and 28, and the court will also take up his request to represent himself. The execution, by firing squad per reports, would be the first US military execution since 1961.
items.notes: 'First since 1961' and firing squad per AP/qz headlines via secondary summaries; CBS Austin did not state them.

items.text: Golden State Medical Supply of Camarillo, Calif., is recalling one lot (GS069303, exp. January 2030) of prescription 800 mg ibuprofen tablets nationwide because aluminium particles may be on the tablets; it says harm is unlikely and no adverse events were reported, and wholesaler McKesson was told to quarantine stock. Separately, an FDA Class II recall covers 51,762 units of ORL Labs toothpaste and mouthwash (37 lots) after FDA sampling found progesterone, estradiol or DHEA, attributed to cross-contamination; no illnesses are reported.
items.notes: FDA pages not reached directly. ORL recall began Oct 12 and was classified Nov 6 (reported Nov 26); ibuprofen FDA notice date unknown.

items.text: In a Thanksgiving call with deployed troops, Trump said Iran will never have a nuclear weapon and that the US would absolutely hit the Pickaxe Mountain site if needed, while saying he had seen no real activity there. He called the naval blockade of Iran the greatest ever and said he was working on Iran and Russia-Ukraine peace. He also claimed a 14-icebreaker deal with Finland for the Coast Guard, 200 more F-16s and a possible rise in defence spending toward $1.5 trillion; none of these was detailed or confirmed officially.
items.notes: Third-party transcript, partly edited; figures inconsistent. Treat procurement claims as unverified.

items.text: USTR Jamieson Greer told CNBC that any change to US sectoral (Section 232) tariffs on autos and steel would have to include something for Canada, without saying what. Canadian vehicles face 25% tariffs and Trump has said auto tariffs rise to 50% on Jan 1, 2027. Canada's trade minister Dominic LeBlanc says progress has been made but Ottawa is not about to sign, and expects talks to resume after US Thanksgiving. Canada is not among the 14 economies in the new Section 301 proposal.
items.notes: Greer quotes via The Hub citing CNBC.

items.text: The extraordinary European Council on the 2028–2034 EU budget ended in the early hours of Friday after about 15 hours of talks, with no agreement, Council President António Costa said. Leaders discussed Costa's compromise of €1.58 trillion, against the Commission's €1.76 trillion in 2025 prices. Costa said most states opposed further cuts and a clear majority wanted farm and cohesion funding kept, while net payers led by Germany pushed for reductions. 24 of 27 states backed an extra loan of up to €45bn for Ukraine in 2027 (up to €25bn military, €20bn budget support); Bulgaria will fund only the non-military part, and Slovakia, Czechia and Hungary want to be exempt from interest costs. Leaders return to both issues at the regular December summit; Poland's EU affairs minister Ignacy Niemczycki had said a deal this year would be very difficult and Poland's chief objection is sending 30% of ETS revenue to the EU budget.
items.notes: Outcome per Costa via PAP (Rzeczpospolita, WP) and EU Alive. No direct post-summit statement from Tusk found; on Thursday he posted that a frugal Europe could be a very costly mistake. Niemczycki quotes from Interia (Nov 26) and WP. No specific December date given in sources.

items.text: On the eve of President Karol Nawrocki's deadline, Sejm Marshal Włodzimierz Czarzasty said that if the President vetoes the bill restoring abortion for severe foetal defects, he will ask the Constitutional Tribunal for an interpretation, suggesting the Tribunal could revisit its 2020 ruling. The bill and the Criminal Code amendment partially decriminalising abortion assistance, both passed by the Senate on Nov 6, still await signature or veto. As of Friday morning no decision had been published on them, on the 'rule of law' judges act or on the PIT/CIT rate reform, all due around Nov 27. The President is on an official visit to Argentina and Chile scheduled for Nov 23–27.
items.notes: Czarzasty spoke on Super Express's YouTube channel (via rp.pl). prezydent.pl could not be fetched; no decision found in news searches as of Nov 27 morning. A decision may come later on Nov 27 — the desk should re-check before publishing.

items.text: President Nawrocki met Chilean President José Antonio Kast in Santiago, the first visit by a Polish president in 24 years, after meeting Argentina's Javier Milei in Buenos Aires on Nov 24. Nawrocki said Poland wants an economic and investment presence in Latin America and cited KGHM's Sierra Gorda copper and molybdenum mine as a model to expand; the two discussed mining technology, energy, agriculture, astronomy, cybersecurity and hybrid threats, and reaffirmed support for Ukraine's territorial integrity. Presidential aide Marcin Przydacz said the trip's main aim was lobbying for Poland's permanent G20 seat before the Miami summit. On Friday Nawrocki was due to visit Sierra Gorda and the Extremely Large Telescope site.
items.notes: No agreements reported from either meeting. Itinerary from RMF24 (Nov 22). Interia reports Argentina assured Poland of firm support for its G20 bid (anonymous Chancellery sources).

items.text: Interia, citing anonymous officials in the President's Chancellery and a senior Polish diplomat, reports that Russia may try to block Poland's bid for permanent G20 membership indirectly, through Brazil and possibly India, rather than oppose it openly and anger the US. Permanent membership needs unanimity, and a decision could come at the G20 summit in Miami on Dec 14–15. According to the sources, Argentina firmly supports Poland, Saudi Arabia may, India has so far committed only to cooperating with Poland's G20 work, and Brazil is a likely opponent. The Foreign Ministry's fallback is for Poland to remain a guest for three more years under the UK, South Korea and Mexico presidencies.
items.notes: Based on anonymous sources; picked up by WP and Goniec. Mentions India's position — coordinate with the Poland–India agent to avoid duplication.

items.text: The Warsaw District Court overturned the city hall's refusal to let the right-wing protest camp in front of the Constitutional Tribunal continue after Nov 30. Judge Anna Bonkowska-Kubek said a total ban on an assembly is allowed only in very exceptional cases and authorities must first look for ways to let it go ahead peacefully; the city has 24 hours to appeal. Mayor Rafał Trzaskowski's office had cited a late notification for a 36-day event to Jan 5, tents and a stage on the pavement and bike path, police closing Aleja Szucha, and the protected buildings nearby. The camp, organised by Warsaw's Gazeta Polska Club since mid-September, opposes the Sejm-elected judges' takeover of the Tribunal; PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński called the ruling very optimistic and summoned supporters to a rally there on Sunday at 15:00.
items.notes: Judge's reasoning per WP overnight roundup. Framing differs: right-leaning Do Rzeczy headlines it as Kaczyński triumphing over a Trzaskowski ban; Kaczyński called the ban 'authoritarianism'; the city stresses residents' disruption and safety. Whether the city appealed was not known at time of writing.

items.text: Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, who heads the Constitutional Tribunal according to the Sejm-elected judges, said in a communiqué that the law provides no appeal against a Tribunal General Assembly resolution consenting to prosecute a judge, after reports that the Supreme Court's Professional Responsibility Chamber had registered appeals by Bogdan Święczkowski and Bartłomiej Sochański against losing their immunity. She said that chamber has no jurisdiction over Tribunal judges. Separately, PM's Chancellery head Jan Grabiec said the Tribunal's bills will be paid through an auxiliary account at Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego while the National Bank of Poland keeps all Tribunal payment orders frozen. Święczkowski told RMF FM that NBP governor Adam Glapiński's freeze was a huge mistake and said he would take his case to MEPs in Strasbourg.
items.notes: BGK account detail from Grabiec on TVN24+ as relayed by Wieści24 (an opinion piece); not independently confirmed. The Interia Święczkowski interview's date is unclear (page cached Nov 27). Whether the Supreme Court chamber has ruled on the appeals is not stated.

items.text: Konfederacja said it is notifying prosecutors about Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński after a TVN24+ investigation found that he raised about 724,000 zł for his 2023 Sejm campaign, the most of any PO candidate, and that more than two-thirds came from 113 people who worked for, or later joined, state companies and institutions overseen by Civic Coalition (KO). Konfederacja MP Michał Wawer pointed to possible paid protection under Article 230 of the Criminal Code, while calling it only a lead. Razem's Adrian Zandberg called for Kierwiński's resignation, and KO senator Grzegorz Schetyna said the matter must be clarified. Kierwiński did not comment, and a new no-confidence motion is barred until February because the Sejm rejected one in early November.
items.notes: Original TVN24+ report is paywalled; figures via RMF24 and WP. Notably the investigation comes from a liberal outlet usually seen as government-friendly; right-wing outlets (niezalezna.pl, Radio Maryja) frame it as nominations for donors. No wrongdoing has been established.

items.text: IMGW kept first-degree snowfall warnings for Friday in Lower Silesia, Opole, Silesia, Lesser Poland and Subcarpathia, forecasting 10–15 cm of new snow and up to 20 cm in the foothills, easing by evening. Daytime temperatures are -3 to -1°C in the south and around 0°C in central Poland, with wind-chill of -5 to -8°C, local drifting and slippery roads in the south and east. Forecasters expect a high-pressure block and Arctic air from Saturday, with frost of -10 to -20°C possible in places on Nov 29–30.
items.notes: Warnings per IMGW via Dziennik.pl and rp.pl. The weekend frost figure comes from model-based forecasts (GEM, CFSv2) reported by Dziennik.pl, not from IMGW. No national tally of outages or fire-brigade call-outs for Nov 26–27 was found.

items.text: The Energy Minister's notice set maximum pump prices for Friday Nov 27 at 5.81 zł/l for Pb95 (from 5.82), 6.47 zł/l for Pb98 (from 6.48) and 7.12 zł/l for diesel (from 7.15). All three caps fell again, though by less than on previous days.
items.notes: Monitor Polski text not fetched; figures via Forsal citing the ministry notice.

items.text: GDDKiA opened the missing connectors at the S7/S52 Mistrzejowice interchange on Thursday 26 Nov, closing Kraków's expressway ring road (about 57 km: roughly 27 km of A4, 18 km of S52 and 12 km of S7). Drivers can now go directly between the northern bypass (S52) and the S7 from Nowa Huta in both directions. The junction opened under construction-site traffic rules: the left lane towards Warsaw stays closed between the Nowa Huta and Mistrzejowice junctions and finishing works continue, with all works due by end-2026. The Mistrzejowice II links to Okulickiego and Petőfiego streets are due by the end of the year. Kraków is the second Polish city after Łódź with a full expressway ring.
items.notes: Interia gives junction figures (11 ramps, ~10 km of carriageways, ~26,500 t of steel); the ~1.7bn zł cost is for the whole S7 Widoma–Kraków section, not the junction. No outlet gave the exact hour traffic was let on. Also KRKnews (Gibała spoke at the opening).

items.text: At the Mistrzejowice opening, Deputy PM Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said the government is interested in rail transport for big cities and that a metro or an alternative could matter; Infrastructure Minister Dariusz Klimczak said he would back whatever solution cities choose, including Kraków. Neither gave an amount or written commitment. Deputy mayor Karol Wałachowski said there is still no clear government commitment, and Mayor Łukasz Gibała repeated that metro work stays paused until central funding is guaranteed. No outlet reported the outcome of the planned Gibała–Klimczak meeting. Separately, Kazimierz Barczyk, head of the Association of Municipalities and Counties of Małopolska, wrote to the mayor and councillors asking that metro preparations continue and be funded in the 2027 budget.
items.notes: TVN24 (Anna Winiarska, 26 Nov 08:36) adds that Kosiniak-Kamysz says Klimczak asked the funds ministry to reserve money in the next EU budget period. Puls Krakowa (11:35) said talks with the government 'might' take place that day; no later report confirms they did. Barczyk letter: KRKnews.

items.text: IMGW issued a first-degree warning for heavy snow for Kraków and all of Małopolska from 18:00 Thu 26 Nov to 18:00 Fri 27 Nov (80% probability), with 10-15 cm of new snow and up to 20 cm locally. City waste and cleaning company MPO sent 218 of its more than 280 winter machines out on Thursday, including 57 salt spreaders; MPK shortened routes of bus lines 245, 215 and 214 because of the snow. Snow-covered roads and truck jams were reported on Thursday evening in Wadowice county. Forecasts point to sharp frost after the snow, around -8°C on Saturday and down to about -12°C on Sunday night, which could ice the roads.
items.notes: Frost figures are forecasts quoted by Puls Krakowa. Tatras at avalanche level 2; part of the Perć Akademików trail on Babia Góra closed (Radio Kraków). Friday-morning transit impact not yet reported when researched.

items.text: Sensors on a waste-collection truck flagged radiation about 300% above the permitted level in waste at the Rydygier Specialist Hospital in Nowa Huta on Thursday morning (alert at 10:21). Firefighters' chemical-ecological unit, police with dogs, the environmental inspectorate WIOŚ and sanepid searched the waste store for several hours and traced the source to a single iodine-isotope capsule, of the kind used to treat thyroid disease, which had ended up in a bin by accident. The container was outside the main building, the hospital was not evacuated, and the hospital says patients were not at risk. The State Atomic Energy Agency (PAA) was notified.
items.notes: No dose figures or PAA findings published; who discarded the capsule is not stated.

items.text: Eryk Stasielak, head of the Małopolska branch of the National Prosecutor's Office, told PAP that about 250 witnesses to the 7 Nov attack have been questioned and that prosecutors are examining a 'foreign thread', without giving details, as well as whether the attacker acted alone or was inspired or urged on by others. The motive is still not established. Toxicology results, which will show whether he was under the influence of drugs, are expected in two to three weeks; autopsy and weapons/ammunition expert opinions are pending. Prosecutors are also examining how he obtained his firearms permit (issued in January 2026; first gun bought in March).
items.notes: Based on a PAP interview; the nature of the 'foreign thread' is not explained. Do Rzeczy and Goniec carried the same PAP material (could not be fetched). RMF24 link not read in full.

items.text: From Saturday 5 Dec, tram lines 1, 3, 8 and 20 will run every 10 minutes (instead of usually 20) on Saturdays and holidays between about 10:00 and 19:00. Line 78, which replaces lines 8 and 20 while ul. Karmelicka is under works, also runs more often, and line 12 will run every 10 minutes on holidays from 9:00 to 20:00. The city calls the change permanent.
items.notes: Single outlet, citing city information; check the ZTP/MPK timetable notice.

items.text: The Christmas market on Rynek Główny opens for trading on Friday 27 Nov, with about 100 trade and food kiosks, and runs into early January. The official opening is on Saturday 28 Nov at 12:00, with the Trebunie-Tutki band. Holders of the Karta Krakowska get 20% off at food stalls and a 5 zł carousel ticket. It is the first big event on the square since the 7 Nov attack.
items.notes: End date differs by source: LoveKraków says 1 Jan 2027, other guides 6 Jan. Hours from Kraków Portal: Sun–Thu 9:00–22:00, Fri–Sat to 23:00. No report on security measures found. Puls Krakowa (23 Nov) said resident discounts could reach 40%; not checked.

items.text: Kraków City Hall has filed a cassation complaint with the Supreme Administrative Court (NSA) against the October ruling by the Kraków administrative court (WSA), which found former mayor Aleksander Miszalski's order dismissing MOCAK director Adam Budak invalid. Mayor Łukasz Gibała has since appointed Grzegorz Kuźma director from 1 Dec without a competition. Budak's lawyer, Wojciech Krawiec, says he is considering challenging that appointment in court.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Publication date not shown in the fetched text; article ID places it around 25-26 Nov. Not confirmed by a second outlet.

items.text: The residents' group Komitet S7 dla Mieszkańców has proposed its own route for the S7 between Kraków and Myślenice that bypasses Myślenice and the Raba valley to the east, 49-60.7 km long with 13 accompanying roads. It says it assessed over 1,200 variants to limit demolitions. The study was handed to GDDKiA in Warsaw on 6 Nov, sent to the Infrastructure Ministry, and presented online on 25 Nov. Deputy PM Kosiniak-Kamysz said on 26 Nov that no variant opposed by residents will go through.
items.notes: GDDKiA's response to the citizens' study is not reported. Only the headline of the Kosiniak-Kamysz article could be read.

items.text: Kamil W., a suspect in the August beating in Nowa Huta of 36-year-old Jakub C. ('Yankes'), who died more than three months later, was brought from Slovakia on 25 Nov under a European Arrest Warrant. He is charged with taking part in a beating with a dangerous object (up to eight years), denies it and refused to give a statement; prosecutors asked the court to extend his custody. Forensic experts found the death was not a direct result of the injuries or of illness, so the prosecutor ordered a supplementary opinion.
items.notes: Detainees are linked to the 'Młoda Ferajna' group (LoveKraków).

items.text: The city's green-space authority ZZM has started renovating the Planty between the Barbakan and the Florian Gate: damaged paths, the surfaces marking the former city walls, paving under benches and fences, due to be finished by the end of April 2027. The separate conservation of the Barbakan (over 1.53m zł, mostly from the Social Committee for the Restoration of Kraków's Monuments) runs until the end of 2027, and the Barbakan stays open to visitors.
items.notes: No cost given for the Planty works; path closures not described.

items.text: Firefighters and WIOŚ dealt with an oily yellowish film on the Sudół stream near ul. Grochowska on Wednesday afternoon. The inspectorate says it was most likely food-grade fat; it was broken up with neutraliser and collected with sorbent mats, with no further spread. No WIOŚ-supervised industrial plant was found nearby as a source.
items.notes: Substance type not confirmed by lab tests.

items.text: The Ekstraklasa League Commission upheld Cracovia's protest and cancelled the yellow card shown to Ajdin Hasić in the 3-1 win over Jagiellonia, after a binding opinion from the PZPN referees' college. Hasić stays on two bookings rather than three, further from a suspension.

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said on X (Nov 26) that the government has asked the Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene Parliament for 'essential Government Business': the Lok Sabha from Monday Nov 30 and the Rajya Sabha from Wednesday Dec 2, with both Houses possibly concluding Dec 3. Because the Monsoon Session was adjourned sine die on Aug 13 but never prorogued, this is technically an extension of it and needs only short notice. Rijiju gave no agenda, but PTI and ETV Bharat sources say the Union Cabinet meets on Nov 27 at 1 pm to take up a revised delimitation-linked women's reservation package, the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, which would raise the Lok Sabha cap from 550 to 850 and let the one-third women's quota apply from 2029 using the 2011 Census. A similar package failed on Apr 17 (298 for, 230 against, 54 short of the two-thirds needed). Aaj Tak's count puts the NDA about 41 short in the Lok Sabha and 11 short in the Rajya Sabha. Winter Session dates have still not been announced.
items.outlet: ETV Bharat / Business Standard (PTI) / The Week
items.notes: Contested. Opposition (Congress's Jairam Ramesh and Manish Tewari, CPI(M)'s John Brittas) calls it a bid to 'manufacture' a two-thirds majority through defections (20 rebel TMC and 6 Sena-UBT MPs, per Aaj Tak) and says the session is about delimitation, not women's quota; Ramesh (Nov 27, The Federal) calls the CEC 'compromised'. Government side, via an unnamed BJP leader in The Week, says it is determined to pass the bill and will address DMK and southern concerns. NCP(SP) issued a whip; Supriya Sule is open to support if it is in the 'national interest'; AAP will oppose. Seat-formula details (50% rise vs keeping 1971 proportions) are unconfirmed. Swarajya's coverage found is from April only; no right-leaning outlet piece on the Nov announcement was found. Bill details from Business Standard explainer (Vrinda Goel, Nov 27). Cabinet outcome not yet known at time of writing.

items.text: Mahanadi Coalfields, Coal India's largest subsidiary, listed on Nov 27 at ₹134 on the NSE (1.47% below its ₹136 issue price) and ₹133.15 on the BSE (−2.10%). The ₹8,981-crore IPO was entirely an offer for sale by Coal India, so the company gets no proceeds. It was subscribed 1.52 times, with only qualified institutional buyers (4.95x) fully subscribing. It is the third Coal India unit to list, after Bharat Coking Coal (January) and CMPDIL (March).
items.notes: Opening prices only; no closing price at time of writing. The BS text says 'premium' once, which is a typo; the figures show a discount.

items.text: The Sensex closed Nov 26 up about 390 points (0.46%) at 84,328.59 and the Nifty 50 rose about 65 points (0.25%) to 25,884.50, after giving up much of an early rally as Brent crude climbed toward $90 on West Asia tensions. IT stocks led (Nifty IT +3.66%; HCL Tech, TCS, Infosys) while FMCG fell 0.94%. Foreign investors were net buyers of about ₹5,843 crore on Thursday, per Times Now Navbharat. The rupee weakened to about 92.4 per dollar and slipped further to 92.62 in early trade on Nov 27 as Brent rose above $95 after ship attacks near Hormuz.
items.notes: Rupee close differs: Aaj Tak says 92.44, Times Now Navbharat 92.38. FII figure from Times Now Navbharat only.

items.text: Tamil Nadu told the Supreme Court on Nov 25 that its Nov 20 order letting the Karthigai lamp be lit at the Thiruparankundram hilltop pillar (deepathoon) could not be carried out because the temple administration refused. Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna's affidavit blamed the trustees' resolution to keep to custom and offered an apology. The bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi declined to start contempt on its own but allowed petitions. Several contempt pleas followed: one by petitioner Rama Ravikumar names 11 officials and trustees (including HR&CE Commissioner T.G. Vinay, the Collector and the Madurai police commissioner), seeks a Chief Secretary's affidavit on any role of Chief Minister Vijay and his ministers, and asks for a new lamp date within seven days. The Hindu reports the pleas are listed on Nov 27.
items.outlet: LawChakra / Bar & Bench / The Hindu (via BozokMedia)
items.notes: Nov 25 hearing not previously logged. Trustees call the pillar a British-era survey stone; some sthanikars say in filings they were not consulted (The Hindu via BozokMedia, secondary copy). Organiser frames the pleas as exposing the Vijay government's defiance. Main appeals stay listed for January 2027. Outcome of the Nov 27 listing not yet known.

items.text: The Election Commission wrote to 27 states and UTs on Nov 25 telling them to check electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Summary Revision for 'probable incorrect or erroneous entries' by matching names, relatives, birth dates, mobile numbers and photos against Special Intensive Revision (SIR) data. Booth-level officers must visit flagged voters, and corrections can be made only through a Form 8 signed by the elector, not by automated matching alone. States named include UP, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa, Manipur, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Bihar and Assam. Claims close Dec 11 and final rolls are due Jan 4, 2027 (West Bengal's SIR rolls Jan 16).
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: Based on The Federal's account of the EC letter; the letter itself was not found on eci.gov.in. Context: UP researchers flagged 19,000 duplicates; Karnataka CEO admitted multiple-EPIC lapses on Nov 8. The Delhi CEO's office separately said no eligible voter will be left out (ETV Bharat, Nov 26).

items.text: Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and the R.D. Tata Trust, which together hold about 66% of Tata Sons, filed suits in the Bombay High Court against Tata Sons and six directors over N. Chandrasekaran's reappointment to a third term as executive chairman on Sept 17. They argue the presiding director's casting vote could not override the Articles of Association requirement that a majority of trust-nominated directors back the decision (Noel Tata opposed; Venu Srinivasan supported). They seek a declaration that the resolution is void, an injunction, a bar on casting votes when nominee directors split (including at a Nov 30 board meeting), and ₹65 crore in damages with interest. Justice Arif Doctor recused; Justice Abhay Ahuja listed the matter for Nov 27.
items.notes: No Tata Sons response reported. Bloomberg (paywalled) also reports the suits. Outcome of Nov 27 hearing not yet known.

items.text: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav released the party's manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election in Lucknow on Nov 26. Its promises include 25 lakh government jobs, ₹5 meals at Samajwadi canteens, a ₹40,000 annual pension for elderly women, workers and artisans, a legal MSP guarantee for 23 crops and milk, a ₹15,000 crore fund to pay sugarcane growers within 24 hours, reopening 26,000 primary schools, a caste census and 50% reservation for Dalit and PDA groups in government contracts up to ₹50 crore. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya called it a fraud. The same day Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad held a joint rally in Lucknow.
items.notes: Maurya reaction via Aaj Tak live blog. Some outlets also mention ₹5,000 a month for jobless graduates (Aaj Tak, NationPress), which ETV Bharat does not list.

items.text: The Centre told the Delhi High Court on Nov 26 that Maharashtra Police issued a Look Out Circular on Nov 22–23 against Saurav Das, chief spokesperson of the Cockroach Janta Party, who was stopped at Delhi airport from flying to London for a Dec 1 Oxford Union talk. ASG Chetan Sharma said discrepancies in his passport over place of birth and parentage, under inquiry since August, may bear on his citizenship. The MEA says the Chennai passport office issued a show-cause notice on Nov 23 and advised him not to use the passport until he replies. Das's counsel Akhil Sibal argued travel is a fundamental right and no LOC had been shared. Justice Amit Mahajan sought the Centre's reply and listed the case for Dec 9.
items.notes: Contested. Das calls it political vendetta; Organiser (RSS-linked) presents the MEA account as authoritative and his claim as overreach. LiveLaw and The Week report both sides. Spelling varies (Saurav/Sourav).

items.text: China's defence ministry spokesperson Senior Colonel Chen Xi said on Nov 26 that the India–China border situation 'remains generally stable' and that both sides are communicating through diplomatic and military channels, including general-level talks held earlier this month. He also repeated China's claim to Arunachal Pradesh as 'Zangnan'. The talks followed reports of aggressive Chinese troop posturing in the Upper Subansiri area. Chen also criticised the recent India–Japan 2+2 defence agreement as part of Japanese 'remilitarisation'.
items.outlet: PTI (via ThePrint, Daily Excelsior) / The Week
items.notes: No MEA response found. The Global Times carries the Chinese framing.

items.text: A Supreme Court bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran accepted FSSAI's proposed timeline of about four months to draft and finalise front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPNL) rules for packaged food, in a single phase, as reasonable. The court told FSSAI to avoid delay and said that if food companies and health advocates cannot agree, public health and consumer interest must prevail. The case was brought by the trust 3S and Our Health Society.
items.notes: Label format (warning vs star rating) not stated in the report. A secondary site says 'within 10 weeks'; PTI says about four months.

items.text: The Home Ministry handed the probe into the early-November IED blast on the Anupgarh–Suratgarh railway line near Ramsinghpur in Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan, about 40 km from the Pakistan border, to the National Investigation Agency. Police treat it as a terror case and have arrested three men, Mahakdeep, Davinder Singh and Hardeep Singh, who will move to NIA custody. Police say the explosives and weapons were dropped by drone from across the border near Jaisalmer and Gurdaspur. The blast went off about 45 minutes after a passenger train passed, with no injuries reported.
items.notes: Blast was about Nov 3 (FPJ). Pakistan drone link is a police claim, not verified; Aaj Samaaj reports RDX from Pakistan. No NIA statement found.

items.text: Delhi's average AQI was 226 ('poor') at 7 am on Nov 26, down from 228 a day earlier, with three of 56 reporting stations 'very poor' (Anand Vihar 327, DTU 308, North Campus 302). GRAP Stage II remains in force across Delhi-NCR, as it has since Nov 2. Sirsa in Haryana was the worst of 286 cities at 368. Safdarjung recorded the season's coldest morning so far (10°C) on Nov 25, and dense-fog alerts cover 13 states and UTs in north India.
items.notes: NationPress headline gives city AQI 319, which appears to be the Anand Vihar figure; CPCB average per BS is 226.

items.text: Voting began at 7 am on Nov 27 for 268 seats in 16 Tripura urban local bodies, including the Agartala Municipal Corporation, with about 5.56 lakh voters and 733 candidates (BJP 266, CPI(M) 228, Congress 201). The BJP already won 77 seats in five other civic bodies unopposed; CPI(M) alleges its candidates were intimidated into withdrawing, which the State Election Commission denies. Counting is on Dec 3.
items.notes: Turnout not yet reported at time of writing; early reports said polling was peaceful.

items.text: SBI Research's Ecowrap recommends a 25 basis point repo rate hike at the RBI's December policy meeting rather than a bigger move, warning that a jumbo hike could trigger capital outflows, rupee instability and growth concerns. Ahead of official July–September GDP data due Nov 30, a Reuters poll of 43 economists expects 7.6% growth, SBI Research about 7.8%, against the RBI's 7.2% projection.
items.notes: Poll figures via a secondary aggregator (The Open Press); Reuters original not read.

items.text: The Home Ministry issued a gazette notification on Nov 26 empowering states and UTs to act under UAPA against the Islamic Research Foundation founded by Zakir Naik, following its Nov 13 extension of the ban for five years.
items.notes: Notification not located on egazette.gov.in; single live-blog item.
